definitions.explanation: The legal or political right of a region, group, or institution to govern itself independently.

examples.japanese: {住民|じゅうみん}は{自治権|じちけん}を{求|もと}めている。
その{地域|ちいき}には{広|ひろ}い{自治権|じちけん}が{認|みと}められている。
examples.english: That region is granted broad autonomy.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}の{自治権|じちけん}は{憲法|けんぽう}で{保障|ほしょう}されている。
examples.english: University autonomy is guaranteed by the constitution.

examples.japanese: {植民地|しょくみんち}の{人々|ひとびと}は{長年|ながねん}にわたって{自治権|じちけん}の{獲得|かくとく}のために{闘|たたか}ってきた。
examples.english: The people of the colony fought for years to obtain the right of self-governance.

notes:
Composed of {自治|じち} (self-governance) + {権|けん} (right). Used in political, legal, and academic contexts to discuss the right of communities, regions, or institutions to manage their own affairs without external control.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自治権|じちけん}を{認|みと}める: recognize the right to self-governance
- {自治権|じちけん}を{求|もと}める: demand autonomy
- {自治権|じちけん}を{獲得|かくとく}する: obtain autonomy
- {自治権|じちけん}の{拡大|かくだい}: expansion of autonomy
- {地方|ちほう}{自治権|じちけん}: local autonomy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自治|じち}: self-governance (the concept itself, without the "right" nuance)
- {自主権|じしゅけん}: sovereignty, independence (broader)
- {自律|じりつ}: self-regulation, autonomy (often personal or organizational)
- {独立|どくりつ}: independence (complete separation, stronger than autonomy)
